title: Painting the Walls
summary: Given two arrays, cost and time, representing the cost and time to paint n walls, find the minimum cost to paint all walls using either a paid painter for the specified cost and time, or a free painter for any wall at no cost, with the free painter only used if the paid painter is busy.
statement: Given two arrays, cost and time, representing the cost and time to paint n walls, find the minimum cost to paint all walls using either a paid painter for the specified cost and time, or a free painter for any wall at no cost, with the free painter only used if the paid painter is busy.
constraints: Paying painter i costs cost[i] and paints one wall while a free painter can paint time[i] additional walls.
The free painter works only while a paid painter is active.
Return the minimum cost to finish all n walls.
hints: Hiring painter i provides capacity for 1+time[i] completed walls.
Use 0/1 knapsack where dp[j] is minimum cost to cover j walls.
Update covered counts backward and cap them at n.
Every hired subset has additive cost and coverage; backward transitions enumerate each subset once and retain its cheapest capped coverage.
editorial: Every hired subset has additive cost and coverage; backward transitions enumerate each subset once and retain its cheapest capped coverage.

tests.explanation: Hiring painter zero alone covers two walls; hiring painter three covers three, totaling cost three for all four.
Two cost-two painters cover all four walls for total four.
